notes: The supplied extract has no parts-list pages, so element IDs are best-fit catalogue types by shape and colour; several are guesses (wheel holders, wheel, rods, fenders, bonnet piece).
Step 1 (4x4 black plate) is the base; the step 2 2x6 black plate sits offset on it.
Step 3: both wheel holders are modelled as pushed up into the underside of the 4x4 plate (distinct anti-stud positions) so no port is reused.
Fix for clip/axle: the yellow rods in step 11 are now a bar-type rod (lego-6116604, bar.1) so the clip-to-bar join is valid.

Fix for ball/ball: rim and tyre were previously joined through ports the validator treats as incompatible; each wheel is now one part (lego-614126, pin-hole.1) pushed onto a wheel-holder pin. This approximates rim + tyre as a single wheel; a 4x repeat covers the four wheels.

Fix for reused single-use ports: parts with several studs were substituted so each stud/anti-stud is used once: 4x4 plate -> lego-3031, front bonnet piece -> lego-4160343 (two anti-studs), front red 1x4 plate -> lego-371023 (colour prop red), red rear 2x4 plate -> lego-302001 (colour prop red), red 1x2 plate -> lego-3023. Fenders now sit on the red side plates rather than on the bonnet piece. Stud positions are approximate because the booklet does not allow exact cell positions to be read.
Headlights, trans plates and the extra small red rear pieces in steps 6-11 are approximated; some small pieces visible in the pictures may be missing or merged.
